title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
tldr: An independent imaging method built only on calibration-proof measurements recovers the ring around M87's black hole, 42.2 microarcseconds across, implying a mass of about 6.5 billion Suns.
byline: Samuel Lai, Nithyanandan Thyagarajan, O. Ivy Wong et al.

title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
tldr: A newly found 3.95-billion-year-old rock in North China formed from ocean crust buried to mantle depths, suggesting a short-lived subduction event early in Earth's history.
byline: Hangqiang Xie, Chunyan Dong, Pengchuan Li et al.

title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
tldr: Tidal turbine blades made of flexible rubber matched the energy yield of rigid blades with active pitch control while cutting fatigue-causing load swings by up to a third.
byline: Zhehong Zhang, Junchen Tan, Eric-Carin Neba et al.

title: Euclid's first major data release maps more than 900 million galaxies and about 15,000 likely gravitational lenses
tldr: ESA's Euclid telescope has published its first major data release, covering about 14% of its planned survey, with over 900 million galaxies, 60 million possible quasars and roughly 15,000 probable strong lenses.
byline: The Guardian, ESA Euclid

title: ESA's Hera begins close-up study of the asteroid pair NASA's DART mission hit in 2022
tldr: ESA says its Hera spacecraft is now studying the asteroid Didymos and its moonlet Dimorphos from 25 to 30 kilometres away, starting a "crash site investigation" of the first asteroid deflection test.
byline: Phys.org (Associated Press), ESA

title: The two most notorious "forever chemicals" have fallen by about 30% in England's rivers, but replacements are appearing
tldr: An Environment Agency report finds PFOS and PFOA concentrations in English rivers fell 30% and 29% over a decade, while short-chain substitutes such as trifluoroacetic acid are now widespread.
byline: New Scientist, BBC News

title: Bound states in the continuum through quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
tldr: Physicists created a molecular state of two lithium atoms that stays bound above the energy at which it should fall apart, by making two collision resonances cancel each other's escape routes.
byline: Alexander Guthmann, Louisa Marie Kienesberger, Felix Lang et al.

title: Majorana edge reconstruction and the ν = 5/2 non-Abelian thermal Hall puzzle
tldr: Theorists propose that the edge of the 5/2 quantum Hall state reorganises itself into stripes, which would reconcile a long-running clash between heat-flow experiments and numerical predictions.
byline: Tevž LotričTaige WangMichael P. ZaletelSteven H. SimonS. A. ParameswaranaRudolf Peierls Centre for Theoretical Physics, Oxford OX1 3PU, United Kingdombhttps://ror.org/01an7q238Department of Physics et al. · Rudolf Peierls Centre for Theoretical Physics, University of Oxford; Department of Physics, University of California at Berkeley

title: Gemini and Webb find the oldest compact pair of quasars, two black holes that grew too big too early
tldr: Astronomers found two actively feeding supermassive black holes, 1.5 billion and 400 million solar masses, only 18,100 light-years apart just 900 million years after the Big Bang, the oldest compact quasar pair known.
byline: NSF NOIRLab, Phys.org

title: NASA studies show how the LISA observatory could find planets with gravitational waves
tldr: Two papers in The Astrophysical Journal work out how the planned LISA space observatory could detect giant planets orbiting pairs of white dwarfs, and how the Webb telescope could confirm them.
byline: NASA

title: A vanished chemical fingerprint dates the switch to modern-style plate tectonics to 2.5 billion years ago
tldr: Curtin University geologists found that a chemical signature of crust formed about 4 billion years ago appears in rocks worldwide until 2.5 billion years ago, then disappears, marking a shift towards large-scale crustal recycling.
byline: Curtin University, Phys.org

title: Ultrafast Meissner-levitated microrotor
tldr: A 30-micrometre magnet levitated above a superconductor at 4.2 K spins at 2.3 MHz, the fastest magnetically levitated rotor reported, with friction so low it serves as a pressure gauge and a dark-matter probe.
byline: Joel K. Jose, Andrea Marchese, Marion Cromb et al.

title: Photonic entanglement swapping with remote quantum dots
tldr: Physicists entangled two photons that never interacted by combining photon pairs from two separate on-demand quantum dots, reaching a swapping fidelity of 0.71, a step toward quantum repeaters built from deterministic light sources.
byline: Mattia Beccaceci, Giuseppe Ronco, Fabrizio Cienzo et al. · Sapienza Università di Roma; Politecnico di Milano; Johannes Kepler University Linz; University of Würzburg; Paderborn University; Karlsruhe Institute of Technology

title: Modified Newtonian Dynamics and galaxy clusters
tldr: Applied to 106 X-ray-mapped galaxy clusters, Modified Newtonian Dynamics cuts the needed unseen mass 4 to 10 times, leaving a compact residual that could be dark ordinary matter.
byline: Francoise Combesahttps://ror.org/00cpdar66Observatoire de Paris, Laboratoire d’étude de l’Univers et des phénomènes eXtrêmes, Collège de France et al. · Observatoire de Paris; Collège de France; CNRS

title: Chandra finds a black hole or neutron star behind a star's repeating outbursts
tldr: X-ray data show that a massive star that flares every 113 days is being stripped by a hidden black hole or neutron star, the first X-ray detection of this kind of erupting star.
byline: NASA

title: Global CO2 emissions are set to fall slightly in 2026, but mostly because of the Iran war's oil shock
tldr: The Global Carbon Budget projects fossil CO2 emissions down 0.4% to 38.2 billion tonnes in 2026, which its authors attribute largely to the oil shock from the Iran war rather than climate policy.
byline: New Scientist, Phys.org

title: Physicists image "ultraquantum" turbulence in a cloud of ultracold atoms
tldr: A Cambridge team directly imaged tangled vortex lines in a turbulent quantum gas, and found it relaxes much like denser liquid helium does.
byline: New Scientist, Physical Review Letters

title: Scaling up chemical recycling: High-yield polyolefin pyrolysis to liquid hydrocarbons using iron single atom catalysts
tldr: An iron single-atom catalyst converts 97% of polyolefin plastic to liquid hydrocarbons with 94% yield, and works at kilogram scale.
byline: Guo-Ping Lu, Xueping Zhang, Kai Xu et al.

title: Revisiting the additionality and durability of carbon uptake in large-scale ocean iron fertilization
tldr: Simulations suggest ocean iron fertilization removes carbon most durably in the Southern Ocean, but only about 30 petagrams of carbon over a century, less than earlier estimates.
byline: Kyung-Min Noh, Xiao Liu, Charles Stock et al.

title: Persistent bistability of Nordic Seas overflow waters over 800,000 years
tldr: An 800,000-year reconstruction of a deep North Atlantic current finds it flips between weak glacial and strong interglacial modes, with abrupt collapses and slower recoveries.
byline: Nathan Stevenard, Aline Govin, Catherine Kissel et al.

title: NASA commits to PROMISE, a nuclear-powered rover built from Mars spares, for the Moon's south pole
tldr: NASA is building PROMISE, a six-wheeled, nuclear-powered rover assembled partly from Curiosity and Perseverance spare parts, to scout ice and resources near the Moon's south pole, with a launch targeted for late 2028.
byline: NASA, ScienceDaily

title: Berkeley Earth says 2026 is very likely the hottest year on record as COP31 opens
tldr: Berkeley Earth is 95% confident 2026 will beat 2024's record, while the WMO's more cautious update puts it among the four warmest years, with a strengthening El Niño pushing 2027 higher.
byline: BBC News, World Meteorological Organization

title: Glacial abrupt transitions in ocean circulation were much slower than ice-core records imply
tldr: Asian cave records show ice-age abrupt warmings took over a century, far slower than Greenland ice cores imply, because Greenland captured a fast atmospheric change, not the ocean's pace.
byline: Xiyu Dong, Xu Zhang, Yuchen Sun et al.

title: Stacked porous NiTi structure with low cost and ultrahigh fatigue life for elastocaloric cooling
tldr: Stamping honeycomb chips from nitinol sheets and stacking them yields a cooling structure that survived more than 100 million cycles and delivers 3850 watts per kilogram, at about a tenth of the usual fabrication cost.
byline: Changfeng Su, Yang Li, Zhongzheng Deng et al.

title: Seafloor geodesy delineates fast megathrust relocking after the giant 2011 Tohoku earthquake
tldr: Fourteen years of seafloor measurements show the fault that produced Japan's 2011 magnitude 9 Tohoku earthquake has already returned to a locked state similar to before the quake.
byline: Fumiaki Tomita, Tianhaozhe Sun, Motoyuki Kido et al.

title: China's space station cools a cloud of atoms to a record 9.7 picokelvin
tldr: Researchers aboard China's Tiangong station cooled about 20,000 rubidium atoms to an equivalent 9.7 picokelvin, about four times below the previous record, and watched the cloud expand for seven seconds.
byline: Phys.org, Chinese Academy of Sciences

title: The Arctic polar vortex is breaking down weeks earlier than ever observed
tldr: Meteorologists say the stratospheric polar vortex is weakening in early November, the earliest disruption on record, but the cause and any effect on winter weather remain uncertain.
byline: BBC Weather, Phys.org (AFP)

title: Mantle currents may have helped carve the Great Unconformity, geologists' biggest gap in the rock record
tldr: Simulations of mantle convection over the past billion years suggest slow uplift of continents, followed by glacial scouring, helped create the Great Unconformity.
byline: Phys.org (University of Wollongong), Ars Technica

title: Three-way circulation–soil moisture–temperature feedbacks amplify the most extreme mid-latitudinal heat waves
tldr: A three-way feedback between drying soils, high-pressure systems and heat appears to make the most extreme midlatitude heat waves about 10% hotter, and warming makes the trigger threshold easier to cross.
byline: Yinglin Tian, Jiangong Liu, Yu Huang et al. · Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research; International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis; Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology

title: Equivalence of pseudogap and pairing energy in a cuprate high-temperature superconductor
tldr: Shot-noise measurements in a bismuth-based cuprate suggest the pseudogap energy equals the energy at which electrons begin pairing, tying a mysterious phase to superconductivity's building block.
byline: Jiasen Niu, Maialen Ortego Larrazabal, Thomas Gozlinski et al. · Utrecht University; Leiden University; Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich

title: Quantum gas microscopy of three-flavor Hubbard systems
tldr: Researchers built the first tunable three-component Hubbard system from ultracold atoms and imaged it atom by atom, observing a Mott insulator and competing magnetic correlations.
byline: Jirayu Mongkolkiattichai, Liyu Liu, Sohail Dasgupta et al. · University of Hamburg; Rice University

title: The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity
tldr: Models of slow mantle flow suggest continents rose for hundreds of millions of years and then sank, which would erase and then bury the rock record behind the Great Unconformity.
byline: Santosh Dhungana, Nicolas Flament

title: Imaging exoplanets below the telescope stability limit
tldr: A physics-based model of Webb's camera, tuned with the gradient descent used to train neural networks, cuts noise in exoplanet images and revealed a planet that had gone unseen at one wavelength.
byline: Rodrigo Ferrer-Chavez, Jason J. Wang, Katherine L. Bouman et al.

title: NASA's Swift gamma-ray observatory ends its 22-year mission with a fiery re-entry
tldr: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory, which tracked more than 2,000 gamma-ray bursts, was predicted to fall out of orbit on 4 November after a failed rescue attempt, and NASA now lists it as having re-entered.
byline: The Guardian, NASA

title: A hidden companion star may be stirring Betelgeuse's atmosphere
tldr: Radio observations from the VLA and ALMA suggest a close companion star, Siwarha, distorts the atmosphere of the red supergiant Betelgeuse, which has otherwise recovered from its Great Dimming.
byline: ScienceDaily (ALMA release), The Astronomical Journal

title: Uranium cubes show Germany's last wartime reactor was far short of what it needed
tldr: A PNAS Nexus analysis of surviving uranium cubes and archives finds the B8 reactor would have needed 1,292 to 1,775 cubes, far more than the 664 used, contradicting Heisenberg's claim that it was nearly critical.
byline: Ars Technica, PNAS Nexus

title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
tldr: Cryogenic atom probe tomography with deuterium tracers gives the first direct observation of hydrogen dissolved in the gaps between metal atoms, and shows the metal's makeup decides where it sits.
byline: Chao Huang, Saiyu Liu, Wenting Lv et al. · University of Sydney

title: Enigmatic HCl detections as a potential signature of igneous activity on Mars
tldr: Seasonal hydrogen chloride spikes above fresh fissures on Mars's Alba Mons suggest gas seeping from hot magma, a possible sign that Mars is dormant rather than dead.
byline: Alexander Trokhimovskiy, Daniel Mège, Oleg Korablev et al. · Space Research Centre of the Polish Academy of Sciences

title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
tldr: Evidence of chirality in manganese telluride supports altermagnetism as a real third class of magnetism that sits between ferromagnets and antiferromagnets.
byline: Daniel Jost, Resham Babu Regmi, Eder G. Lomeli et al. · SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory

title: Chemical traces of blood found in a 115-million-year-old dinosaur bone
tldr: A team led by Curtin University reports red blood cell-like structures and heme molecules inside the leg bone of a 115-million-year-old Brazilian dinosaur, the first chemical evidence of blood in a dinosaur.
byline: Phys.org, The Conversation, Popular Science

title: LHCb sees first evidence of the rarest beauty-particle decay yet observed
tldr: The upgraded LHCb experiment at CERN reports 3.2-sigma evidence for a beauty-particle decay into two muons that occurs about once per ten billion decays, consistent with the Standard Model.
byline: BBC, University of Cambridge, Phys.org

title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial
tldr: In a 90-patient phase 2 trial, ivonescimab plus chemotherapy before and after surgery gave a 70.1% major pathological response in resectable lung cancer.
byline: Xiaoliang Zhao, Bin Zhang, Chenguang Li et al. · Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital, The Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University

title: An AI-native experimental laboratory for autonomous biomolecular operations
tldr: AutoDNA, an AI-run laboratory, coordinates over 20 instruments across more than 11,000 steps to carry out DNA synthesis, amplification and sequencing with minimal human intervention.
byline: Mingyu Wu, Zhaoguo Wang, Jiabin Wang et al.

title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
tldr: Copper complexes of heteroaryl sulfones split apart when hit by visible light, releasing carbon radicals that enable fluoroalkylation of arenes and alkynes.
byline: Zhiqiang Wei, Xiang Li, Lin Xiao et al. · Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, ShanghaiTech University
